name: Zak Kuhr

views.text: Coaching offense first shows a defensive coach what spread and option teams want.
Prepare the calls, then step back and let the players play.
The playoffs are the time to turn up the pressure and trust the corners in man.
Study a runner's style all the way back to college to know what he wants to do.
Doubters and believers both fuel the work; commit fully to whatever role you are given.
A defense that loses the run game in the biggest game has to rebuild that first.

signatures: credits his support system and the players before himself
answers questions about his rise by talking about the role he was handed
brings up detailed opponent tendencies when asked about a game plan

motivation.want: to prove he earned the coordinator title on merit
motivation.fear: being remembered as a stopgap who got the job by circumstance

voice: Driven and confident but deferential; he hands credit to his support system and players and speaks in detail about opponents. Public coverage of his own voice is thin.

evidence.summary: Before he first calls the defense: a Giants assistant in 2024, four years on Vrabel's Tennessee staff, 11 college seasons largely on offense (including Texas State coordinator); Vrabel says his offensive background helps against spread and RPO teams and calls him a superstar.

Before the Super Bowl: he became the de facto coordinator when Williams was treated for cancer, added new wrinkles, and the defense allowed two playoff touchdowns; a linebacker says he lets players play and trusts them to make every call right; he credits his support system and says doubters and believers both drive him.

The interim tag comes off at 37 as Williams moves to a senior role; the defense allowed 18.8 points a game, fourth in the league, and was strong against the run until the Super Bowl. Little on personality.

Official promotion: he ran the defense for the final 20 games, kept the split-safety four-man-front system, raised the playoff blitz rate from about 28 to 44 percent and played more man; players praise his detail and clear messages, such as studying Kenneth Walker's running back to college. Vrabel calls him fantastic.
